# OpacityLock

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Editing` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public enum OpacityLock
```

Whether a paint command may write partial alpha. Locked does *not* mean "no alpha": erasing is how a sprite gets its shape and layers have to composite over one another, so a fully opaque rectangle per layer would make stacking meaningless. It means *binary* alpha — every painted pixel comes out fully opaque or fully erased, nothing between.

## Remarks

[`OpacityLock.Locked`](Nfty.Core.Editing.OpacityLock.md#f-locked) is the zero value on purpose: it is what `default` yields, so a command constructed without saying anything about opacity gets the safe mode. This is an editor setting and nothing else — no manifest field, no schema change, no archive affected.

## Values

- <span id="f-locked"></span>`Locked = 0` - Binary alpha. Every pixel a command writes is snapped to fully opaque (255) or fully erased (0); the pixels it does not touch, and everything `Undo` restores, are left exactly as they were.
- <span id="f-unlocked"></span>`Unlocked = 1` - Partial alpha is written through as the command computed it. Semi-transparent pixels do not voxelize cleanly, which is why this is never the default.
